# Lines that reach a private macOS interface, which `privacy-check.py private` allows, as
# `<path>: <token>`. A hit (dlopen, dlsym, a PrivateFrameworks path or @_silgen_name) is allowed
# when its file equals <path> and the line contains <token>. Each private API sits behind one
# wrapper per API, and every entry was agreed with the maintainer for that module (see
# CLAUDE.md, "Private API only by exception, per module"). A new entry needs the maintainer's
# decision and says why.
#
# The menu bar manager's own interfaces. MenuBarClientCore is the macOS 27 framework that
# conceals the menu bar's items.
holzBar/MenuBar/MacOS27/MenuBarAssessmentAssertion27.swift: dlopen
holzBar/MenuBar/MacOS27/MenuBarAssessmentAssertion27.swift: PrivateFrameworks
# WindowServer's functions for the menu bar's windows and spaces.
Shared/Bridging/Shims.swift: @_silgen_name
#
# The Accessory alerts module reads accessory batteries through IOPSCopyPowerSourcesByType,
# looked up at run time (agreed 2026-10-16).
holzBar/MenuBar/NotchHub/AccessoryAlerts/AccessoryBatterySource.swift: dlsym
#
# The Display controls module sets brightness through DisplayServices, which Apple does not
# document: brightness has no public API (agreed 2026-10-09). The wrapper loads it on first
# use and only while the module's Brightness setting is on.
holzBar/MenuBar/NotchHub/DisplayControls/DisplayServicesBrightness.swift: dlopen
holzBar/MenuBar/NotchHub/DisplayControls/DisplayServicesBrightness.swift: dlsym
holzBar/MenuBar/NotchHub/DisplayControls/DisplayServicesBrightness.swift: PrivateFrameworks
#
# The Now Playing module's Read all apps reads what any app plays through MediaRemote, which
# Apple does not document and only lets Apple's own platform binaries use. The helper framework
# loads it at run time inside /usr/bin/perl and is the only file that names it (agreed
# 2026-10-31; CLAUDE.md, Private API in modules). The bridge names no private API.
NowPlayingRemote/NowPlayingRemote.swift: dlopen
NowPlayingRemote/NowPlayingRemote.swift: dlsym
NowPlayingRemote/NowPlayingRemote.swift: PrivateFrameworks
